name: Kingdom of England
description: The English kingdom ruled successively by English, Danish, Norman, Angevin, Lancastrian, Yorkist, Tudor and Stuart monarchs.

name: Kingdom of Alba / Scotland
description: The Gaelic kingdom of Alba, known as Scotland in English from the eleventh century.

name: Kingdom of Strathclyde / Cumbria
description: British-speaking kingdom centred on the Clyde, extending south towards Carlisle; absorbed by the Scottish kings during the eleventh century.

name: Welsh kingdoms and principalities
description: The native Welsh polities (Gwynedd, Powys, Deheubarth, Morgannwg and others), shown together because their shifting internal boundaries cannot be mapped defensibly at this scale.

name: Anglo-Norman marcher lordships
description: Lordships in Wales conquered by Anglo-Norman barons, held with quasi-regal rights outside the English shire system.

name: English Crown in Wales (Principality and March)
description: After 1283–84 Wales was ruled by the English Crown through the Principality of Wales, with the marcher lordships retaining their own jurisdictions until 1536.

name: Kingdom of the Isles (Norse-Gaelic)
altNames: Kingdom of Mann and the Isles
description: Norse-Gaelic kingdom of the Hebrides (with the Isle of Man, outside this map), under Norwegian overlordship until the Treaty of Perth (1266).

name: Earldom of Orkney (under the Norwegian crown)
description: Norse earldom of Orkney and Shetland, held under the kings of Norway (later Denmark–Norway) until pledged to Scotland in 1468–69; its earls also held Caithness.

name: Commonwealth of England, Scotland and Ireland
description: The republican regime following the execution of Charles I; Scotland was incorporated by the Tender of Union (1652) and the Ordinance of Union (1654).

name: Kingdom of Great Britain
description: Created by the Acts of Union of 1706–07 uniting the kingdoms of England and Scotland.

name: United Kingdom
description: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland from 1801 (Northern Ireland from 1922). Only Great Britain is shown on this map.
